You are cosmic-ext-nightlight's architect, for this one job: nobody else is working here now, so you can rearrange it. Take apart the files agents edit over and over, so that engineers working at once on different things change different files instead of the same ones, and their branches merge without an integrator.

The files Ferrivide has seen agents edit most here, most first:
- README.md: changed by 15 merged tasks of 15 engineers in 14 days
- src/main.rs: changed by 12 merged tasks of 12 engineers in 14 days
- Cargo.toml: changed by 11 merged tasks of 11 engineers in 14 days
- Cargo.lock: changed by 6 merged tasks of 6 engineers in 14 days
- docs/RELEASING.md: changed by 6 merged tasks of 6 engineers in 14 days
- .github/workflows/release.yml: changed by 5 merged tasks of 5 engineers in 14 days
- CHANGELOG.md: changed by 4 merged tasks of 4 engineers in 14 days
- justfile: changed by 4 merged tasks of 4 engineers in 14 days
- src/gamma.rs: changed by 4 merged tasks of 4 engineers in 14 days
- .gitignore: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- data/io.github.cosmic_ext.Nightlight.desktop: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- scripts/publish-apt.sh: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- src/location.rs: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days
- src/solar.rs: changed by 2 merged tasks of 2 engineers in 14 days

1. Measure. Check that list against the git history: the files changed most often and by the most different pieces of work, the files that change together, and why each keeps being edited (which kinds of change land in it).
2. Split. Where several kinds of work share a file, give each its own file, joined at compile time (a module of its own, its tests beside it). Where a file must know every kind of work (message dispatch, settings, event routing, a list of tests), make it a table or list that each part adds a line to from its own file, so adding a feature doesn't edit the shared one. Behaviour doesn't change: move code, don't rewrite it, keep every test passing, and commit in small steps.
3. Report. Say which files you split into which, and which of the list you left alone and why.

Leave generated and project-wide files (Cargo.lock, the README and the like) as they are. Stop at what the history justifies: a split of a file nobody keeps editing isn't worth making.

Second job: bring the project up to the Rust standards (RS1 to RS8, in your instructions as the rust-development skill; the project has no standards file of its own). The user gave no direction for this work: use the standards, the findings and the issues below.
No open issue from Compliance is about structure.

a. Measure first. Run the rust_smells tool on the whole tree (whole: true) and keep its counts: oversized files and impls, types spread over many impl blocks, fields always borrowed apart, borrow-ending clones, mem::take across calls, allocations in loops, unsafe. These are your "before" numbers. Read the project's requirements and contract too: they bind what you change.
b. Pin down behaviour before you move anything (RS6): the project's tests where they pin the results, and for code whose output you restructure, a check that old and new give the same output on fixed inputs, with iteration order made deterministic. Delete the old code once they match.
c. Reorganize toward the standards, most measured payoff first, in small commits: one large state struct into disjoint sub-structs, each with the impl that owns it (RS1, RS7); a kind field and a long if chain back into an enum or trait (RS3); clones that only ended a borrow removed by reshaping the data (RS1); a large crate split only where the measured incremental check time (cargo check after a one-line edit, before and after) gains. Move code, don't rewrite it: behaviour doesn't change and every test still passes. Don't split a file by line count alone, and leave generated files alone.
d. Measure again. Run rust_smells on the whole tree once more for your "after" numbers.

Your closing report_status says which standards (RS1 to RS8) the project now meets, which remain and why each does, with the scan's counts before and after, side by side.

Your closing report_status is published as your report, in the project's Reports tab (Architecture): put which files you divided up and why in its summary and decisions, and what changed in its files. Engineers start only once your work is merged. If nothing is worth dividing, commit nothing, say why, and say plainly in its summary that you have nothing left to do; an interim report_status doesn't end your turn's work. Once your work is merged (or you finish with nothing to merge), you're discarded.
I'll start by measuring: the git history, the tree, the smell scan, and the project's requirements.

# cosmic-ext-nightlight: what the agents learned

What the agents working here learned, kept by Ferrivide for the agents after them and for you. Core goes to every agent it's for, with every request; Reference is read when needed.

## Core

### Applet

- The gamma backend runs on a dedicated worker thread (Worker in src/main.rs); the UI talks to it with Task::perform and a oneshot. State is saved with cosmic::cosmic_config::Config get/set, key 'enabled', version 1. Futures come from cosmic::iced::futures. Not tested live: if cosmic-comp lacks zwlr_gamma_control, the icon stays off and the error goes to stderr. The user wants gamma set directly t…
- libcosmic is pinned by rev in Cargo.toml and the justfile builds with --locked; bump the rev on purpose. Not verified live: cosmic-comp advertising zwlr_gamma_control, and the desktop file's Categories on a COSMIC session. <!-- k2 · 2026-11-12 · Project manager -->
- Right-click popup: cosmic::widget::mouse_area around applet.icon_button, then a Task from cosmic::task::message(cosmic::Action::Surface(app_popup::<App>(..))); on_close_requested must return a PopupClosed message. The popup id logic is the pure helper popup_after_close. Not tested on a live panel. <!-- k6 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files src/main.rs@4cd191c4dbf8 -->
- Temperature is saved under config key 'temperature' (Kelvin, clamped to 1900-6500 on load). The worker request carries Option<u32> (Some = enable at that Kelvin, None = disable). A slider move while a request is in flight sets retune_pending and is applied once on the reply, if still enabled. Not tested on a live panel. <!-- k7 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files src/main.rs@3d0c90a99063 -->
- Schedule: config keys schedule_on, schedule_start, schedule_end (minutes since midnight). Pure logic is Schedule::wants_on and schedule_step in src/main.rs; a 20 s subscription ticks only while schedule_on. It acts only when the window state changes (and at startup, enable or edit), so manual toggles hold; a failed scheduled switch is retried on the next tick. Local time comes from chrono (clock…
- Auto mode: pure logic is in src/solar.rs (sun times, sin^2 ramp, kelvin_for_percent, auto_step) and src/location.rs (timezone coordinates from zone.tab or zone1970.tab). Config keys auto_on, location_custom, location_lat, location_lon. The 20 s tick drives it. Ramp percent 0 disables gamma rather than applying 6500 K. A slider move in auto mode resets auto_last so the new target applies at once.…

### Packaging

- `just deb` runs `cargo deb --locked` (needs `cargo install cargo-deb`) and writes target/debian/*.deb. Config is in Cargo.toml [package.metadata.deb]. Depends is `$auto, cosmic-panel, cosmic-comp`; the cosmic-* package names are unchecked against a COSMIC apt repo. The libc6 floor comes from the build host, so build on the oldest target distro. <!-- k3 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files Carg…
- Releases: .github/workflows/release.yml has build (no secrets), sign (environment `release`) and publish (contents: write) jobs. just and cargo-deb are pinned by hand to exact versions. The README fingerprint placeholder must be replaced with the real signing-key fingerprint before the first v* tag; the build job fails while it is there. <!-- k4 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files README.md@b…
- release.yml fails if README.md contains the fingerprint placeholder text (grep for 'FINGERPRINT-TO-BE-FILLED-IN'). Don't write that exact token anywhere else in the README, or a filled-in README would still fail. <!-- k5 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files README.md@1db6ccdc9ac2, .github/workflows/release.yml@9f6c5479b29d -->
- libcosmic's `applet` feature links GPL-3.0-only crates from pop-os/cosmic-panel (cosmic-panel-config, xdg-shell-wrapper-config). Their Cargo.toml has no license field, so license tools show them blank. Check with `cargo tree -i cosmic-panel-config`. <!-- k10 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files Cargo.toml@f4b6cf88e97d -->
- Release state on GitHub can be read without credentials: curl https://api.github.com/repos/deepthinker2001/cosmic-ext-nightlight/actions/runs, then each run's jobs_url and check-run annotations give each job's failure reason. As of 2026-11-13 no release has published the apt repository (gh-pages is empty). <!-- k11 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files .github/workflows/release.yml@b79f9a952618…
- scripts/publish-apt.sh can be tested locally without a real key: make a throwaway ed25519 key in a temporary GNUPGHOME and a dummy .deb with dpkg-deb --build, then run the script on an empty site folder. <!-- k12 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files scripts/publish-apt.sh@9a1a0f53d0d3 -->
- THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES is generated by `just notices` (scripts/gen-third-party-notices.py) from Cargo.lock; regenerate it when Cargo.lock changes. The script reads license files only from inside the crate or its git checkout, since git checkouts keep symlinks. <!-- k13 · 2026-11-14 · Project manager · files scripts/gen-third-party-notices.py@6ad890bde6ae -->
- Iced-Icons.ttf (compiled in by iced_graphics) holds six Font Awesome glyphs (SIL OFL 1.1, Dave Gandy, picked through Fontello) and the iced logo (MIT). Its OFL notice is data/licenses/OFL-FontAwesome.txt; re-check it if iced_graphics changes the font. cargo-deb is installed here: `cargo deb --locked` then `dpkg-deb -c target/debian/*.deb` checks the package contents (release build about 75 s). <…
- Release is a push to main whose Cargo.toml version has no v<version> tag: the build job decides (step-level ifs), attach creates the tag and release at the built commit and checks the tag's commit, apt signs. The release environment should allow only branch main (no Tag rule); v* tag creation stays restricted, with a bypass for the Actions app (unverified on GitHub). To release: bump version and…

text:
I split `src/main.rs` into seven modules and left every other file on the list alone; the work is committed as `839996f43c`. The same 47 tests pass (1 ignored) and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` are clean, but the applet has not been run on a live panel.

## What was split

`src/main.rs` was 1,191 lines and every feature task landed in it (18 commits). The code is moved verbatim; only visibility, imports and line wrapping changed, which I confirmed by comparing old and new sources line by line.

| New file | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `src/worker.rs` | gamma worker thread, `handle_request` |
| `src/schedule.rs` | `TimeOfDay`, `Schedule`, `schedule_step`, local clock |
| `src/auto.rs` | `auto_percent_now`, `auto_action` |
| `src/switch.rs` | `toggle_request`, `applied`, `Retune` |
| `src/config.rs` | config keys, `Settings` load and save |
| `src/popup.rs` | `popup_content`, `time_picker`, `temperature_hint`, `popup_after_close` |
| `src/app.rs` | `Nightlight`, `AutoState`, `Message`, the `Application` impl |

Each module keeps its own tests. `main.rs` is now the module list, `APP_ID`, `main()` and `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

A new feature still adds lines to `app.rs`, `popup.rs` and `config.rs`, because `Message`, the state struct and `update()` are still one enum, one struct and one match. Breaking those into per-feature pieces would rewrite control flow that can't be verified without a live panel, so I stopped short of it.

## What was left alone

- **`README.md`, `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `justfile`, `.gitignore`, the desktop file, `docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md`:** project-wide or generated. `Cargo.toml`'s edits were dependencies, version and cargo-deb metadata, which I kept there on the understanding that cargo-deb reads it only from `Cargo.toml` (not re-checked).
- **`release.yml`, `docs/RELEASING.md`, `scripts/publish-apt.sh`:** one kind of work, the release process redesigned by successive tasks, so dividing the files would not have kept those tasks apart.
- **`src/gamma.rs`, `src/solar.rs`, `src/location.rs`:** each has one responsibility and is well under the size limits (534, 252 and 188 lines), with few edits.

## Rust standards

| Scan count | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Total findings | 1 | 1 |
| Loop allocations | 1 | 1 |
| All other kinds | 0 | 0 |

The scan itself did not report an oversized file before, though `main.rs` was over RS7's 1,000-line mark; the largest file is now `gamma.rs` at 534 lines.

- **Met:** RS1, RS2, RS3, RS5, RS6, RS7 and RS8.
- **RS4:** the one remaining finding is a false positive, now at `src/worker.rs:46`. `GammaBackend::new` runs once per connection, not per request, so I did not reshape the code to quiet it.

I did not split the crate or measure check times: at about 2,200 lines there is nothing to gain. I have nothing left to do once this is merged.

[7:29 a.m. MST]

[Ferrivide] A scan of your change to Rust files found 1 smell the Rust standards (the rust-development skill) cover. Fix what you agree is a problem, or say in your closing report why it stays; this note comes once for each.
- src/worker.rs:46 [loop-allocation] `handle_request` is called inside a loop in `spawn`, and does `Vec::new` through `GammaBackend::new` (src/gamma.rs:324) on every call (fix: RS4. Hot paths allocate nothing; see RS4)

This finding stays, and nothing changes in the code. It is the same one the scan reported before the split (then at `src/main.rs:78`); it only moved to `src/worker.rs:46` with the code.

It is not a real hot-path allocation:

- **Not on every call:** `handle_request` calls `GammaBackend::new` only while the backend is `None`, which is once per Wayland connection. Later requests reuse the cached backend.
- **Not a hot loop:** the worker loop runs once per user or timer request (a toggle, a slider move, a 20-second tick), not per frame.
- **No allocation at that line anyway:** `Vec::new` does not allocate until something is pushed.

An earlier session already wrote this reasoning into the comment above `handle_request`. Reshaping the code just to quiet the scan would be a rewrite with no gain, against the "move, don't rewrite" rule for this job.

My closing report already records this under RS4, so the report stands as published: `src/main.rs` split into seven modules in commit `839996f43c`, 47 tests passing, and nothing left for me to do once it is merged.
